title: Discrete logarithms in finite fields

problem.name: Discrete logarithms in finite fields
problem.statement_latex: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, an element $g$ of order $r$, and $h\in\langle g\rangle$, find $x\in\mathbb Z/r\mathbb Z$ with $g^x=h$. The input length is $\Theta(\log q)$ plus the field representation. Prime-field Diffie--Hellman is the principal cryptographic application. The explicit-field comparison uses quantum gate complexity and classical bit complexity; the black-box comparison counts group operations.
problem.statement_text: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, an element $g$ of order $r$, and $h\in\langle g\rangle$, find $x\in\mathbb Z/r\mathbb Z$ with $g^x=h$. quantum.headline_latex: $O(n^3)$ gates and $O(n)$ logical qubits, Shor discrete logarithms.
quantum.details_latex: For $n=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, this conventional bound includes reversible field exponentiation and Fourier sampling; fast multiplication improves the arithmetic cost. The group-operation query count is polynomial in $n$. The output is the classical exponent $x$, with constant success probability amplified by repetition.

classical.headline_latex: $L_q[1/3,(64/9)^{1/3}]$ heuristic time in general large prime fields, number field sieve discrete logarithms.
classical.details_latex: The bound includes relation collection, sparse linear algebra and individual-logarithm descent. Special field representations can improve the $L$-constant. For applicable families in small fixed characteristic, Barbulescu--Gaudry--Joux--Thom\'e and subsequent rigorous developments give quasi-polynomial time $\exp((\log\log q)^{O(1)})$. The characteristic and field representation therefore determine the matched classical comparator.

strength.description_latex: Subexponential to polynomial for large prime fields; quasi-polynomial to polynomial in the stated small-characteristic families. The quantum mechanism is abelian Fourier sampling.

evidence.description_latex: Strong conditional evidence under the corresponding classical discrete-logarithm hardness assumption; generic-group lower bounds apply to the separately specified oracle model.

hardware.description_latex: Cryptographic fields require fault-tolerant reversible arithmetic. The data and arithmetic workspace use $O(n)$ logical qubits in space-efficient implementations, with polynomially many coherent field multiplications. Physical-qubit counts depend on the chosen arithmetic circuits and error-correction architecture.
